tunisia.text: Friday couscous, brik straight out of the pan, and harissa on everything.

zambia.text: Maize nshima with relish, dried kapenta from the lakes, and fresh bream out of the Zambezi.

zimbabwe.text: Sadza with relish, and meat over coals wherever there is a fire and company.

image.alt: rock paintings on the Tsodilo hills, Botswana

botswana.text: Four thousand paintings on four hills the San call the resting place of the gods.

image.alt: the National Museum building in Gaborone, Botswana

botswana.text: Independent since 1966, and the one African country that used its diamonds well.
botswana.title: Diamonds and Democracy

image.alt: the Sultan's Palace at Foumban with its museum of the Bamoun kings, Cameroon

image.alt: volcanic rock spires rising from farmland at Rhumsiki in the Mandara mountains, Cameroon

image.alt: the colonial quarter of Grand-Bassam, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire.text: The first colonial capital, on a sandbar between lagoon and ocean, and now a world site.
cote-divoire.title: Grand-Bassam

image.alt: the basilica of Our Lady of Peace at Yamoussoukro, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire.text: A basilica larger than Saint Peter's, built in the founder's home village.
cote-divoire.title: Yamoussoukro

image.alt: painted tomb walls in the Valley of the Kings, Egypt

egypt.title: The Valley of the Kings

image.alt: the hypostyle hall columns at Karnak, Egypt

egypt.title: Karnak, Luxor, Abu Simbel

image.alt: the rock-hewn church of Bete Giyorgis at Lalibela, Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: Eleven churches cut down into solid rock in the twelfth century, still in use every day.
ethiopia.title: Lalibela

image.alt: the stone castles of Fasil Ghebbi at Gondar, Ethiopia

ethiopia.title: Aksum and Gondar

image.alt: the door of no return at Elmina castle, Ghana

ghana.text: Cape Coast and Elmina — the doors of no return, kept as they were and not softened.
ghana.title: The Slave Forts

image.alt: a memorial gathering at Cape Coast castle, Ghana

ghana.text: Ghana asked the diaspora to come back, and a great many people did.
ghana.title: The Year of Return

image.alt: the coral ramparts of Fort Jesus above Mombasa old harbour, Kenya

kenya.text: Portuguese, built 1593, taken and retaken nine times — now UNESCO World Heritage above the old harbour.
kenya.title: Fort Jesus, Mombasa

image.alt: carved wooden doors and coral stone alleys in Lamu Old Town, Kenya

kenya.text: The oldest continuously inhabited Swahili settlement, carved doors, coral rag walls and no room for a car.
kenya.title: Lamu Old Town

image.alt: the wooden royal compound at Ambohimanga, Madagascar

madagascar.text: Ambohimanga, the royal hill of the Merina kings above Antananarivo.
madagascar.title: The Rova and the Royal Hills

image.alt: the pirate cemetery on Île Sainte-Marie, Madagascar

madagascar.text: Île Sainte-Marie's pirate cemetery, and the Merina kingdom that unified the island.
madagascar.title: Pirates and Kingdoms

image.alt: the stone steps of the Aapravasi Ghat, Mauritius

mauritius.text: The immigration depot where half a million indentured labourers first landed.
mauritius.title: Aapravasi Ghat

mauritius.text: The mountain where escaped slaves lived at the top, and a world heritage site for that reason.
mauritius.title: Le Morne

image.alt: the earth kasbah of Ait Benhaddou above the river, Morocco

morocco.text: A Roman city on the plain at Volubilis, and Ait Benhaddou standing above the Ounila.
morocco.title: Volubilis and the Kasbahs

image.alt: the tanneries and rooftops of the Fez medina, Morocco

morocco.text: Fez, Marrakesh, Meknes and Rabat — four capitals, each of a different dynasty.
morocco.title: The Imperial Cities

image.alt: the fortress of São Sebastião on Ilha de Moçambique, Mozambique

mozambique.text: The old capital, on a coral island a kilometre long, with a fort at one end.
mozambique.title: Ilha de Moçambique

image.alt: the crumbling colonial buildings of Ibo island, Mozambique

mozambique.text: Ibo, Angoche and Sofala — Indian Ocean trading towns older than the Portuguese.
mozambique.title: The Swahili Coast

namibia.text: Two thousand rock engravings on one hillside, cut into sandstone six thousand years ago.
namibia.title: Twyfelfontein

namibia.text: A diamond town the desert has taken back, and the German colonial coast at Lüderitz.
namibia.title: Kolmanskop and the Coast

nigeria.text: The walls of Benin, and Sungbo's Eredo — a hundred and sixty kilometres of earthworks.
nigeria.title: Benin City and Sungbo's Eredo

nigeria.text: The Benin bronzes are the reason half the museums of Europe have a Nigeria problem.
nigeria.title: The Bronzes

rwanda.text: The reconstructed royal residence at Nyanza, thatched and enormous, with the long-horned Inyambo cattle still kept.
rwanda.title: Nyanza, the King's Palace

rwanda.text: The Kigali Genocide Memorial is where any honest visit to Rwanda starts, and it explains everything that came after.
rwanda.title: Memory and Reconstruction

senegal.text: The island off Dakar, and the house of slaves that stands on it.
senegal.title: Gorée

senegal.text: The old colonial capital on its island in the river mouth, with the Faidherbe bridge.
senegal.title: Saint-Louis

seychelles.text: L'Union Estate on La Digue, with its vanilla, copra mill and colonial house.
seychelles.title: The Plantations

seychelles.text: A thousand kilometres out, with a hundred thousand giant tortoises and almost no people.
seychelles.title: Aldabra

south-africa.text: Twelve kilometres off Cape Town, a political prison for three decades, now guided by the men who were held there.
south-africa.title: Robben Island

south-africa.text: The Sterkfontein caves have produced more early hominin fossils than any other site on the planet.
south-africa.title: The Cradle of Humankind

tanzania.text: Stone Town is UNESCO-listed; Kilwa Kisiwani was the richest port on the Swahili coast six centuries ago.
tanzania.title: Stone Town and Kilwa

tanzania.title: Olduvai and the Coast

tunisia.text: El Jem's amphitheatre seats thirty-five thousand and is standing almost complete.
tunisia.title: Carthage, Dougga, El Jem

tunisia.text: Tunis, Sousse and Kairouan — Kairouan's mosque is among the oldest in the Maghreb.
tunisia.title: The Medinas

image.alt: the great thatched dome of the Kasubi Tombs in Kampala, Uganda

uganda.text: The burial ground of four Buganda kings, thatched, enormous and rebuilt by the clans who have always maintained it.
uganda.title: The Kasubi Tombs

image.alt: royal regalia and drums inside a Buganda kingdom palace

uganda.text: Royal drums, regalia and clan structures that survived the protectorate, the 1966 crisis and the 1970s.
uganda.title: Kingdoms Still Standing

zambia.text: The old colonial capital above the falls, its museum, and the tree where the man himself is said to have camped.
zambia.title: Livingstone

zambia.title: Mosi-oa-Tunya, UNESCO

zimbabwe.text: Eight hundred years old, mortarless, and the largest stone structure south of the Sahara.
zimbabwe.title: Great Zimbabwe

zimbabwe.text: Khami's terraces, and the Matobo hills where Mzilikazi and Rhodes are both buried.
zimbabwe.title: Khami and Matobo

image.alt: San guides walking a Kalahari pan in the morning, Botswana

botswana.text: Tracking with San guides, who will find in an hour what nobody else sees at all.
botswana.title: The Kalahari San

image.alt: a family on a mokoro in the Okavango channels, Botswana

botswana.text: Not a budget destination — but the children will not be sharing a sighting with ten vehicles.
botswana.title: Not the Cheapest, but Quiet

image.alt: a Mafa farmer on the terraced slopes of the Mandara mountains, Cameroon

cameroon.text: Two hundred and fifty ethnic groups and as many languages, from the Mafa terraces of the Mandara to the Fulani of the Sahel.
cameroon.title: Fulani, Mafa and Bamileke

image.alt: villagers and guides repairing a stone section of mountain trail together, Cameroon

cameroon.text: Guides and porters come from the mountain villages in rotation, and the trail money goes back into the village fund.
cameroon.title: Village and Mountain Together

image.alt: Senufo carved figures on a workshop bench, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire.text: Baoulé weaving, Senufo sculpture, and Dan masks from the western hills.
cote-divoire.title: Baoulé, Senufo and Dan

image.alt: children swimming on the lagoon side at Assinie, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire.text: Assinie's sandbar has ocean on one side and calm lagoon on the other, which suits children.
cote-divoire.title: Beach and Lagoon

image.alt: a brightly painted Nubian village on the Nile at Aswan, Egypt

egypt.text: Nubian villages above Aswan and Bedouin communities in the Sinai and the Western Desert.
egypt.title: Nubians and Bedouin

image.alt: a family boarding a Nile cruise boat at Luxor, Egypt

egypt.text: Short internal flights, boats instead of buses, and a story at every stop.
egypt.title: Straightforward with Children

image.alt: a village of the lower Omo valley at the end of the day, Ethiopia

ethiopia.title: Omo Valley

image.alt: a family walking a highland track in northern Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: Cool highland air, short flights between the historic sites, and no malaria at altitude.
ethiopia.title: Highland Travel

image.alt: a weaver working a kente loom in Bonwire, Ghana

ghana.text: Kente weaving in Volta and Ashanti, and the Dagbon drumming traditions of the north.
ghana.title: The Ewe and the Dagomba

image.alt: children playing on a beach on the Ghanaian coast

ghana.text: English-speaking, short distances, and about as gentle an introduction as the continent offers.
ghana.title: Easy First Africa

image.alt: a Samburu warrior with beaded ornaments in the northern drylands, Kenya

kenya.text: Samburu in the northern drylands, Maasai in the south, both still moving cattle between seasonal grazing.
kenya.title: Samburu and Maasai

image.alt: a community conservancy ranger team on patrol near the Maasai Mara, Kenya

kenya.text: Community conservancies lease grazing land back for wildlife, and the lease pays the schools around the Mara.
kenya.title: The Conservancies

image.alt: a family tomb standing in highland Madagascar farmland

madagascar.text: The ancestors are present here in a way that shapes the calendar and the architecture.
madagascar.title: Famadihana and the Ancestors

image.alt: children on a village path in rural Madagascar

madagascar.text: Roads are slow and distances are long — but the children will hold a chameleon.
madagascar.title: Slow, and Worth It

image.alt: a village street in the Mauritian sugar country, Mauritius

mauritius.text: Creole spoken by everyone, Bhojpuri in the villages, and French and English in print.
mauritius.title: Creole and Bhojpuri

image.alt: children playing in a calm Mauritian lagoon, Mauritius

mauritius.text: Flat warm lagoon, no dangerous surf inside the reef, and short drives from anywhere.
mauritius.title: Made for Families

image.alt: a shepherd with his flock on a High Atlas terrace, Morocco

morocco.text: Village life at two thousand metres, where the year is still organised around the snow.
morocco.title: The People of the Atlas

image.alt: a family walking a quiet lane in a Moroccan hill village, Morocco

morocco.text: Short drives, good roads, and a train line down the coast that children enjoy.
morocco.title: Easy Travelling

image.alt: a Makonde carver at work in northern Mozambique

mozambique.text: Makonde carving in the north, and the Makua women's mussiro face paint.
mozambique.title: Makonde and Makua

image.alt: children swimming in shallow water inside a reef, Mozambique

mozambique.text: Shallow, warm and calm inside the reef — as easy a sea as the continent offers.
mozambique.title: Warm Water All Year

seychelles.text: Lagoons inside the reef, no dangerous surf on most beaches, and short boat rides.

south-africa.text: Guided by residents, spending in the neighbourhood, and honest about what apartheid planning actually built.
south-africa.title: Township Tourism, Done Right

tanzania.text: One of the last hunter-gatherer peoples in Africa, speaking a click language unrelated to anything nearby.
tanzania.title: The Hadzabe of Lake Eyasi

tunisia.text: The ksour of Tataouine, and the underground houses of Matmata.
tunisia.title: The Berber South

tunisia.text: Short flights, shallow warm sea, and resorts that have been doing families for decades.
tunisia.title: Two Hours from Europe

image.alt: a Karamojong herder with cattle on the plains of Karamoja, Uganda

uganda.text: The Batwa, forest people of the southwest, and the Karamojong cattle-keepers of the northeast plains.
uganda.title: Batwa and Karamojong

uganda.text: Community walks in Buhoma and Nkuringo, run by the villages that share the forest with the gorillas.
uganda.title: Villages at the Forest Edge

zambia.title: Village Around the Park

image.alt: a community conservation sign at a delta concession, Botswana

botswana.text: Concessions leased through community trusts, so the villages hold the lease and the income.
botswana.title: Community Trusts

image.alt: Eco Tourism in Cameroon

image.alt: a researcher on a forest trail at Taï, Côte d'Ivoire

image.alt: black rhino grazing on the Ol Pejeta conservancy at dawn, Kenya

image.alt: a reforestation nursery beside a Madagascar rainforest park

madagascar.text: Deforestation is the country's crisis, and the parks that work are the ones the villages run.

image.alt: a pink pigeon in Mauritian native forest, Mauritius

image.alt: a park scientist at work in Gorongosa, Mozambique

mozambique.text: Local employment, local science, and a park brought back from nothing — worth understanding.

strands.line: Africa is not one people. It is roughly two thousand languages, and the answer changes at every border and often inside one.
strands.title: People

strands.asks: What is kept, and who keeps it?
strands.line: Kingdoms that still hold court, festivals with a date and a place, and practices that belong to particular communities rather than to a continent.
strands.title: Culture

strands.line: Not a cuisine. Fifty-four of them, argued over, regional inside every country, and mostly cooked at home.
strands.title: Food

strands.line: Work with a technique, a lineage and a place it is made — bronze, cloth, beadwork, clay — and usually a market you can buy it in from the person who made it.
strands.title: Craft

strands.asks: What is it like to live here?
strands.line: Most Africans live in cities and most visitors fly over them. Markets, transport, music, nightlife and the ordinary weekday.
strands.title: Cities

strands.line: What was built, what was survived, and what is deliberately kept — including the parts that are difficult to stand in front of.
strands.title: Heritage

strands.asks: What does a visit do to this place?
strands.line: Who holds the permit, where the money lands, and who is employed. Stated where an operator has said it, and left blank where nobody has.
strands.title: Responsibility
